claims: Google Messages is updating to allow partial text selection.
Partial text selection in Google Messages was spotted in beta version v20260306.
In Google Messages beta version v20260306, users can long-press a message and drag to select text.
In Google Messages beta version v20260306, users can use the traditional full-copy button.
Users can highlight specific text within a message bubble (OTP codes, phone numbers, addresses) instead of copying the entire text string.
Users long-press a message and use the updated context sheet to select text.
The standard "Copy" button remains available for copying everything, notes Android Police.
The partial text selection feature in Google Messages is currently available in a staged rollout to users in the Google Messages beta program (v20260306).
The partial text selection change in Google Messages removes the need for workarounds like pasting full messages into other apps to delete unnecessary parts.
The Google Messages update is designed to behave like Android's standard system-level text selection, say this article.
